problems.location: p.7 Corollary2.2 and proof; Step5 p.9
problems.claim: Every sufficiently small C1 perturbation of each first K sloshing modes on Omega_1/2 has a nodal component isotopic to Sigma.
assumptions: n=3, smooth rounded cylinder, Sigma=unit disk, product metric
beta=1/100, K=3, transverse positive ground mode ell=2
u is any smooth function on closed Omega_1/2
problems.decisive_evidence: w=-c I0(pi beta r)cos(pi t)<=0 for abs(t)<=1/2; for any delta>0 set u=w-eta, 0<eta<delta. C1 difference eta, u<0, no zeros. Mode ordering verified by ground bound9pi^2/800<100 transverse excited lower bound.
problems.counterevidence: Each mode has a regular zero slice inside Omega_3/4, and p13 already supplies C^r convergence on any Omega_tau, tau<1.
problems.impact: False central nodal-persistence corollary breaks Step5 as written; no counterexample to the main existence theorem.
problems.repair: Use Omega_tau with tau>1/2 and select a mode-dependent regular zero slice; use a common tolerance for finite K.
problems.repair_status: Local repair verified; no author adoption established

problems.location: p.8 Step4 definition g_epsilon,h=rho_epsilon,h^2 g_epsilon and Proposition2.4
problems.claim: Displayed family consists of smooth metrics converging to g_epsilon.
assumptions: rho smooth and positive with specified bounds
g_epsilon has jump from g to epsilon^2 g
problems.decisive_evidence: Interface traces rho^2 g and rho^2 epsilon^2 g differ; outside transition family equals epsilon^4 g instead of target epsilon^2 g. Explicit epsilon1/2 rho3/4 gives9/16 versus9/64.
problems.counterevidence: Using original smooth g as base gives the intended corrected family.
problems.impact: Written construction does not deliver a smooth metric; spectral approximation and final theorem step cannot use it.
problems.repair: Set tilde g_epsilon,h=rho^2 g; impose epsilon<=rho<=1 globally, retain interior agreement.
problems.repair_status: Corrected construction and applicability conditions verified; full later publisher proof uninspected

problems.claim: H1 defined by exterior harmonicity alone gives direct sum with H2 and energy orthogonality; full exterior H1 norm uniformly bounded by inside boundary norm.
assumptions: h=(t-1)_+ belongs H1(M), harmonic on Omega complement, zero in Omega and on lateral interface
For secondary bound: compactly supported exterior bump with low weighted Rayleigh quotient
problems.decisive_evidence: Nonzero h lies H1 intersection H2; pairing h with itself has energy at least pi beta^2>0. For psi=1+c epsilon^(-(n-2)/2)z, mixed part=1 and weighted energy bounded, but unweighted exterior gradient diverges.
problems.counterevidence: Construction (4.7) already imposes the missing exterior Neumann condition; AppendixB supports an energy-plus-boundary estimate on the mixed extension, not on all psi.
problems.impact: Core lower min-max bound lacks its asserted orthogonality and uniform estimate.
problems.repair: Restrict H1 by weak exterior Neumann condition; use S<=C(LB+A), epsilon^(n-1)T<=Cepsilon B, absorb boundary triangle inequality to B<=(1+Csqrt(epsilon))A; obtain injective restriction and lower min-max bound.
problems.repair_status: Replacement lower-bound derivation verified in report

problems.source_claim: PDF p7 Corollary 2.2, product definition pp5-7, core invocation p9.
problems.hypotheses_checked: n=3; smooth connected rounded cylinder; transverse separating disk with nonempty boundary; product metric on Omega_2; beta=0.01 and finite K=3; arbitrary smooth C1-close function on closed Omega_1/2.
problems.independent_check: For ell=2, w=-c I0(pi beta r) cos(pi t)<=0 on |t|<=1/2. Subtracting any 0<eta<delta gives a root-free admissible perturbation. The transverse excited branch has eigenvalue >=100 while each first three ground branches is <=pi^2 ell^2 beta/8<=9pi^2/800; strict monotonicity in potential orders them. The reported counterexample does not depend on the source's zero/one indexing inconsistency.
problems.counterevidence_and_repair: For each ell>=1 choose its closest zero t_ell; |t_ell|<=1/2<3/4 and |partial_t w|=(pi ell/2)v_0^ell is bounded below on the compact slice. Finite K permits a common tolerance. Source p13 supplies C^r convergence for every fixed tau<1. This repairs the region and application, not the printed corollary.
problems.dependency: Corollary 2.2 is expressly used in Step5 of Theorem1.2, so the invalid core persistence statement supports Major without refuting the theorem.

problems.source_claim: PDF p8 Step4, with g_epsilon defined on p5.
problems.independent_check: The printed g_epsilon,h=rho^2 g_epsilon retains unequal positive interface traces rho^2 g and epsilon^2 rho^2 g. In the exterior its pointwise limit is epsilon^4 g, not epsilon^2 g. These are failures of the actual stated metric construction, not extraction uncertainty.
problems.counterevidence_and_repair: Replacing the base by smooth g and taking epsilon<=rho<=1 gives smooth metrics converging to the target for fixed epsilon. Uniform ellipticity, compact trace, and unchanged interior elliptic regularity support precisely the scoped local construction repair.
problems.dependency: The final smooth metric and the spectral approximation step depend on this construction. A short correction does not remove its core Major status.

problems.source_claim: PDF pp11-13 equations4.6,4.8,4.11 and lower min-max bound; AppendixB p15.
problems.independent_check: h=(t-1)_+ is H1 on the smooth rounded flat product domain, is harmonic on each exterior component and vanishes on Omega/interface, hence is a nonzero element of both printed spaces. Pairing it with itself yields positive energy. Separately psi=1+c epsilon^(-(n-2)/2)z with compactly supported exterior z has fixed boundary trace, fixed weighted energy, mixed extension1 and divergent unweighted exterior gradient norm. Small c and the positive low-subspace spectral margin give the stated admissible Rayleigh restriction.
problems.counterevidence_and_repair: The actual construction4.7 already imposes exterior Neumann data, which must also enter H1. For the corrected mixed decomposition, S<=C(LB+A) and epsilon^(n-1)T<=C epsilon B yield (1-C sqrt(epsilon))sqrt(B)<=sqrt((1+C epsilon^(n-1))A+C L epsilon^(n-1)B). Absorption gives B<=(1+C sqrt(epsilon))A. If A=0, B=0 and the low-energy condition force psi=0, proving restriction injectivity. Min-max then yields the reported lower bound.
problems.dependency: These false printed inputs are central to Proposition2.3 and Theorem1.2; the replacement proof does not establish author adoption or a false main theorem.
